meta.move: Evidence: the made-up quotation, with a check she can make
meta.expect: Tries one parent defence in one sentence (misremembered, a bad edition), then accepts that a line she can check against the play is evidence; no concession that Owen cheated

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Why does my son have a zero?
I entered the zero before I called you. That was wrong.
Okay. You've said it was wrong, so who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
The essay quotes Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line is not in the play. Here's the full text of Act 3, Scene 2 on my screen. Search it yourself.
Turn the screen. I'll search it myself. And a line misquoted from memory is a mistake in an essay, so what makes it more than that?
It isn't a misremembered line. It isn't anywhere in Hamlet, in any edition. You can search the whole play right now.

I'm writing that down, Hale. A line that isn't in the play still doesn't tell me how it got into the essay, and nobody asked Owen before the zero went in. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You acknowledged that the zero was entered before you called me and that this was wrong. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an answer on who decided it and whether Owen was heard first, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record and that this stays private. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback. She wants the zero withdrawn, nothing on his record and the matter kept quiet, and she wants an answer on who decided the zero. Nothing was agreed, so this is not yet the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4; her time did not run out.
What moved her: You gave her a line from the essay that you said appears nowhere in the play and let her search the text herself, which moved her because it was specific, tied to Owen's work and something she could check.
What cost ground: Nothing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence did not touch that night, since you only raised a line from the essay, so she stayed sharp on procedure. It proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fights so hard.
Try next time: When she asked who decided the zero and whether Owen was heard first, you went straight to the evidence, so answer that question directly and then offer the supervised reassessment in procedure 4.4.
